hypothesis: Implementing an agentic knowledge layer (centralized ingestion, indexing, and retrieval powering RAG agents) will measurably improve task accuracy and reduce completion time for knowledge-intensive workflows across support, sales, HR, and IT compared to agents (or humans) operating on scattered documents and ad-hoc search, without degrading answer freshness or trustworthiness.

baseline.description: Current-state knowledge access without a unified agentic knowledge layer. Workflows rely on manual search or naive per-tool RAG.
conditions: No centralized, cross-domain knowledge index; information resides in siloed systems (e.g., Zendesk/Helpdesk tickets, Confluence/Google Drive docs, CRM notes, HRIS docs, IT runbooks).

Agents (or human operators in the manual baseline workload) access knowledge via:
  - Native search in each system (e.g., Confluence search, Google Drive search), OR
  - A simple, single-source RAG setup per domain (e.g., support bot with its own small vector index, sales bot with a different index), with no shared schema or metadata conventions.
No continuous ingestion agents; indexes or docs are updated manually and irregularly.
No automated deprecation of stale content; outdated docs remain accessible without warnings.
Prompting pattern: agents receive the user query and (optionally) a raw text dump of the few top search results from one system, without unified reranking or metadata-based filtering.

treatment.description: Centralized agentic knowledge layer with ingestion, indexing, and retrieval powering domain agents via a unified RAG API.
components:
Ingestion pipeline:
  - Scheduled and on-demand ingestion agents pulling content from multiple systems: ticketing/support KB, CRM, HRIS/HR KB, IT runbooks, wikis, document stores.
  - Normalization into a common document schema: {id, source_system, source_url, domain, doc_type, title, body, created_at, updated_at, owner, confidentiality_level, tags, validity_start, validity_end (optional), canonical_version_id (optional)}.

Indexing:
  - Central vector index (e.g., using a local vector DB like Chroma/Weaviate/Qdrant) storing embeddings of document chunks plus metadata.
  - Text-chunking strategy (e.g., 512–1024 token windows with overlap).
  - Secondary metadata index (e.g., SQL/NoSQL) to support filtering by domain, doc_type, recency, and confidentiality_level.

Retrieval API:
  - A single retrieval service exposing a function signature like retrieve_knowledge(query, domain, user_role, top_k, filters) returning ranked passages + metadata.
  - Hybrid retrieval (keyword + vector) or at least metadata-aware vector retrieval (filtering by domain, recency, and confidentiality_level).

RAG agent pattern:
  - Domain agents (support, sales, HR, IT) call the shared retrieval API instead of per-domain ad-hoc search.
  - Prompts explicitly separate task instruction, retrieved passages (cited with source IDs/URLs), and answer generation.
  - Agents surface citations and confidence indicators to users.

Freshness/deprecation agents:
  - Continuous ingestion workers detecting new/updated docs via webhooks or polling, updating the central index incrementally.
  - Deprecation agents flagging or downranking documents that are superseded (based on updated_at, canonical_version_id, or explicit deprecation tags) and optionally inserting warnings into responses if only stale content is available.

workloads.name: support_faq_resolution
workloads.description: Agents answering internal or external support questions (e.g., product features, troubleshooting steps, entitlement policies) using the organization's knowledge.

input_set.source: Synthetic and/or anonymized real support tickets and FAQ queries, normalized into a structured dataset.

fields: gold_citations (list of document_ids and span references in the KB)

workloads.baseline_flow: Agent (or human operator for manual variant) uses existing support KB search or per-tool non-centralized RAG, then answers the question without access to cross-domain index.
workloads.treatment_flow: Support agent calls the centralized retrieval API with domain='support' and appropriate metadata filters, uses returned passages to craft an answer with citations.

workloads.name: sales_ops_policy_and_process_lookup
workloads.description: Agents assisting sales or RevOps with questions about pricing rules, discount approvals, contract clauses, and internal process steps.

input_set.source: Synthetic sales policy/process queries derived from real playbooks and approval matrices.

workloads.baseline_flow: Sales agent uses CRM notes, shared drives, or internal wiki search without a unified index; or a narrow sales-only RAG index.
workloads.treatment_flow: Sales agent calls centralized retrieval with domain='sales', filters by doc_type in ['pricing_policy', 'approval_matrix', 'contract_template'], and responds with cited guidance.

workloads.name: hr_it_internal_service_qa
workloads.description: Agents answering employees' HR and IT questions (benefits, PTO, device policies, VPN setup, password reset edge cases).

input_set.source: Synthetic HR/IT queries based on internal policy docs and runbooks.

workloads.baseline_flow: Agent (or human helpdesk analyst) searches HR/IT systems independently (HRIS search, IT runbook wiki search) and responds without the unified layer.
workloads.treatment_flow: HR/IT agent calls centralized retrieval with domain='hr' or 'it' and confidentiality-based filters, and generates an answer with cited policy/runbook sections.

workloads.name: freshness_regression_suite
workloads.description: Targeted set of questions whose correct answers change due to policy/process updates to evaluate knowledge staleness over time.

input_set.source: Designed scenarios where a document is updated or superseded between T0 and T1.

workloads.baseline_flow: Same as other workloads but with no continuous ingestion; indexes/docs are only updated via infrequent manual runs, so many answers remain on gold_answer_T0 even after T1.
workloads.treatment_flow: Continuous ingestion and deprecation agents ensure the central index reflects updates within a defined SLA (e.g., <1 hour), so answers move from gold_answer_T0 to gold_answer_T1 promptly.

model_and_prompting.llm_model: Use the same LLM (e.g., gpt-4.x or equivalent) and version for baseline and treatment runs.
model_and_prompting.system_prompt_base: Consistent base system prompt describing role, formatting, and need to answer strictly from provided knowledge.
model_and_prompting.post_processing: Identical normalization of outputs (e.g., trimming, markdown stripping) across baseline and treatment.

data_and_randomization.dataset_split: Predefine the full task set; use the exact same questions and order for baseline and treatment.
data_and_randomization.train_test_contamination: Ensure evaluation questions and gold answers are not used to fine-tune or prompt-train agents.

access_and_permissions.user_roles: Simulate same user role/permissions for baseline and treatment to avoid differences due to access restrictions.
access_and_permissions.confidentiality_filters: Apply the same confidentiality level filters in both setups; treatment may enforce them centrally via metadata filters, baseline via system-level permissions.

infra_and_runtime.hardware: Run baseline and treatment on the same hardware tier (or same cloud region and instance types).
infra_and_runtime.concurrency: Limit concurrent requests similarly in baseline and treatment when measuring latency.
infra_and_runtime.cache_policy: Either disable caching or apply identical caching rules in both conditions.

metrics.name: answer_exact_match_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of questions where the agent's answer matches the gold_answer_text exactly under strict string or token-level comparison (after normalization).

metrics.name: answer_semantic_accuracy
metrics.definition: Average semantic correctness score (0–1) per answer, computed via independent LLM-as-judge or human raters using a rubric (correct, partially_correct, incorrect).

metrics.name: citation_precision
metrics.definition: Among the citations provided by the agent, the fraction that point to documents/spans deemed relevant and non-misleading for the gold answer.

metrics.name: citation_recall
metrics.definition: Fraction of gold_citations (or equivalent authoritative docs) that are cited or whose content is clearly used in the answer.

metrics.name: task_completion_time_p50
metrics.definition: Median time from question submission to answer completion for automated runs (or time measured for human baselines where applicable).

metrics.name: task_completion_time_p90
metrics.definition: 90th percentile of completion time across questions.

metrics.name: coverage_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of questions for which the agent returns a substantive answer rather than 'I don't know' or equivalent abstention.

metrics.name: hallucination_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of answers judged to contain fabricated or unsupported claims that are not present in any accessible knowledge source.

metrics.name: stale_answer_rate
metrics.definition: For the freshness_regression_suite, fraction of answers that reflect outdated gold_answer_T0 instead of the updated gold_answer_T1 after the change_timestamp + allowed_SLA.

metrics.name: index_update_latency_p50
metrics.definition: Median time from source document update (e.g., wiki change) to that change becoming available in the retrieval index.

metrics.name: index_update_latency_p90
metrics.definition: 90th percentile latency from source update to index availability.

primary.description: At least a 10 percentage-point absolute improvement in semantic answer accuracy across combined workloads.
Median task completion time reduced by at least 30%.

secondary.description: Hallucination rate at most half of baseline.
Stale answer rate reduced by at least 70% on freshness-dependent questions.
Treatment does not degrade citation quality; ideally improves it.

statistical.test_plan: Use two-sided statistical tests (e.g., proportion z-test for binary metrics, Mann-Whitney U or t-test for continuous metrics) to verify that observed differences are unlikely under the null hypothesis (alpha=0.05).
statistical.minimum_effect_size_reporting: Report confidence intervals for key deltas (accuracy, latency). Do not claim success solely based on point estimates if confidence intervals cross zero.

failure_modes.name: query_mismatch_or_overfiltering
failure_modes.description: The centralized retrieval layer applies overly strict metadata filters (e.g., domain or confidentiality filters) causing relevant documents to be excluded, reducing coverage or accuracy.
mitigations: Log queries with zero or low-relevance results and inspect filters.
Implement a fallback retrieval path that relaxes filters when initial results are sparse.
Perform periodic evaluation of recall on a labeled corpus.

failure_modes.name: indexing_or_chunking_errors
failure_modes.description: Documents are incorrectly parsed, chunked, or embedded, leading to missing or incoherent passages in retrieval results.
mitigations: Track ingestion errors and maintain a queue of failed documents.
Spot-check random samples of indexed documents and their chunks.
Include checksum/version metadata to detect and correct malformed records.

failure_modes.name: stale_or_conflicting_docs
failure_modes.description: The central index contains multiple versions of the same policy or runbook; the retrieval layer surfaces obsolete ones, or the agent fails to prefer the canonical version.
mitigations: Use canonical_version_id and validity_start/validity_end metadata.
Deprecation agent downranks or excludes superseded documents.
Prompt the agent to favor the most recent valid document and to flag conflicts.

failure_modes.name: hallucinations_despite_rag
failure_modes.description: Even with relevant passages, the LLM fabricates steps, numerical values, or policies not in the sources.
mitigations: Constrain prompts to 'answer only from provided context; say you don't know otherwise'.
Introduce answer verification heuristics or a judge agent that checks claims against retrieved text.
For high-risk domains (finance/HR), require human review for non-trivial responses.

failure_modes.name: evaluation_bias_or_leakage
failure_modes.description: LLM-as-judge shares biases with the answering model or has seen the gold answers in its prompt, inflating accuracy scores.
mitigations: Use a separate model as judge or human raters for a subset.
Blind the judge to whether an answer came from baseline or treatment.
Randomize answer ordering during evaluation and log decisions.

failure_modes.name: workload_non_representativeness
failure_modes.description: Synthetic or curated questions do not reflect real-world query distribution, leading to misleading performance claims.
mitigations: Sample anonymized real queries where possible.
Validate the synthetic dataset with domain experts.
Report workload composition and acknowledge limitations.

failure_modes.name: infra_bottlenecks_and_latency_noise
failure_modes.description: Differences in system load, network conditions, or caching cause misleading latency comparisons.
mitigations: Run baseline and treatment in alternating blocks under similar load.
Record per-request timestamps, system load metrics, and retry events.
Use robust statistics (median, p90) and avoid overinterpreting small deltas.

services: LLM provider API (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, or local LLM with equivalent quality).
Vector database (e.g., Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, Pinecone).
Document storage/source systems or fixtures (e.g., local file system with markdown/HTML/PDF docs representing support KB, sales policies, HR/IT policies).
Optional: Relational or document database for metadata index (e.g., PostgreSQL, SQLite, MongoDB).

infrastructure.runtime: Python 3.10+ environment with necessary libraries (LLM SDK, vector DB client, HTTP server framework, evaluation tools).
infrastructure.hardware: Single machine or small VM with at least 8 GB RAM for test-scale corpora (exact requirements depend on document volume; experiments should be designed to run on a typical developer laptop or small cloud instance).
infrastructure.network: Internet access if using cloud LLM/vector DB; for fully offline reproducibility, instructions should also provide an option to use a local LLM and local vector DB.

datasets.support_kb: Synthetic or anonymized documentation for product FAQs, troubleshooting, and policies stored as markdown or HTML files with timestamps.
datasets.sales_policies: Pricing sheets, discount approval matrices, and process docs as structured markdown/CSV/JSON.
datasets.hr_policies: PTO, benefits, and HR process documents as markdown/HTML.
datasets.it_runbooks: IT setup and troubleshooting runbooks and policies.
datasets.question_sets: Structured JSON/CSV datasets for each workload (support_faq_resolution, sales_ops_policy_and_process_lookup, hr_it_internal_service_qa, freshness_regression_suite) with fields described in workloads.

run_instructions: 1. Setup the codebase:

1.1. Clone the repository:
       git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/turn-your-company-into-an-agentic-organization
       cd turn-your-company-into-an-agentic-organization
1.2. Navigate to the chapter 12 experiment directory (e.g., experiments/ch12_knowledge_layer_rag).

1.3. Create and activate a Python virtual environment, then install dependencies:
       python -m venv .venv
       source .venv/bin/activate  # or .venv\Scripts\activate on Windows
       pip install -r requirements.txt
1.4. Configure environment variables for LLM and vector DB access (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY, VECTOR_DB_URL). Do not hardcode secrets in the repo.
2. Prepare synthetic or anonymized corpora:

2.1. Populate the data/corpus directory with domain-specific documents:
       - data/corpus/support/*.md
       - data/corpus/sales/*.md
       - data/corpus/hr/*.md
       - data/corpus/it/*.md
2.2. Ensure each document includes metadata in front matter or sidecar JSON (id, domain, doc_type, created_at, updated_at, etc.).
2.3. For freshness experiments, create two versions of some documents (e.g., pricing_v1.md and pricing_v2.md) with different validity periods.
3. Implement and run the baseline setup:

3.1. Baseline A (recommended): Non-centralized simple RAG per domain.
       - Use the script baseline/build_domain_indices.py to create separate vector indices per domain.
       - Launch the baseline agent server (e.g., python baseline/run_baseline_agents.py), which:
         * Exposes endpoints like POST /answer_support, /answer_sales, etc.
         * For each domain, retrieves from its own index only.
   3.2. Alternative baseline: manual/human evaluation (optional) for a subset of workloads. Document procedures and timing method if used.
3.3. Verify baseline answers on a small sample manually to confirm end-to-end correctness (retrieval + answer generation).
4. Implement and run the treatment (agentic knowledge layer):

4.1. Start the ingestion pipeline:
       - Run scripts in treatment/ingestion (e.g., python ingest_corpus.py) to:
         * Parse documents from data/corpus.
         * Normalize to the common document schema.
         * Chunk content and compute embeddings.
         * Upsert into the central vector index and metadata store.

4.2. Launch continuous ingestion and deprecation agents (for freshness workload):
       - Start watchers (e.g., python watch_for_updates.py) that detect source file updates and re-index changed docs.
       - Run deprecation agent (python run_deprecation_agent.py) to mark older versions as deprecated based on naming or metadata.

4.3. Start the retrieval API service:
       - Run python treatment/run_knowledge_service.py
       - This should expose an HTTP endpoint POST /retrieve_knowledge that accepts query, domain, user_role, top_k, and filters, and returns ranked passages + metadata.

4.4. Start domain agents that use the central knowledge layer:
       - Run python treatment/run_domain_agents.py
       - This service exposes endpoints like POST /answer with payload {domain, question_text, user_role}, internally calling /retrieve_knowledge and the LLM.
5. Run evaluation for both baseline and treatment:
5.1. Load evaluation question sets from data/eval/*.json (one file per workload).

5.2. For each workload and condition (baseline, treatment):
       - Use runner scripts like python eval/run_eval.py --condition=baseline --workload=support_faq_resolution
         and python eval/run_eval.py --condition=treatment --workload=support_faq_resolution.
       - Configure number of repetitions (e.g., --repeats=3) and random_seed=42 for reproducibility.

5.3. Store raw outputs in structured JSONL files (e.g., results/baseline/support_run1.jsonl, results/treatment/support_run1.jsonl) including:
       - question_id, condition, workload, raw_answer_text, citations, start_time, end_time, retrieved_docs, retrieval_latency_ms, llm_latency_ms.
6. Score answers and compute metrics:

6.1. Use scoring scripts (e.g., python eval/score_answers.py) to compute:
       - answer_exact_match_rate
       - answer_semantic_accuracy (via LLM-as-judge or human rating JSON files)
       - citation_precision and citation_recall
       - hallucination_rate
       - stale_answer_rate (for freshness_regression_suite)
       - coverage_rate
       - task_completion_time_p50/p90
6.2. Aggregate per-workload metrics into a single summary table comparing baseline vs. treatment with confidence intervals and p-values for key metrics.
7. Analyze results and validate assumptions:
7.1. Generate plots/tables (e.g., in a Jupyter notebook notebooks/ch12_analysis.ipynb) visualizing accuracy vs. latency, hallucination vs. coverage, and stale answer rates over time.
7.2. Manually inspect a sample of incorrect or hallucinated answers to understand failure modes and annotate whether they stem from retrieval gaps, indexing issues, or LLM behavior.
7.3. Document findings, including any deviations from expected success_criteria, and capture them in a markdown report (reports/ch12_experiment_report.md).
8. Reproducibility checklist:
8.1. Ensure exact model version identifiers, hyperparameters, and dataset commit hashes are recorded in the report.
8.2. Tag the repository with a release (e.g., ch12-knowledge-layer-rag-v1) referencing the scripts, configs, and data used.
8.3. Optionally, provide a docker-compose configuration to spin up vector DB, metadata DB, and services in a single command.

fields.run_id: string, unique identifier for each full experiment run (e.g., UUID).
fields.date_utc: ISO 8601 timestamp of the run start.
fields.vector_db: string, name and version of the vector DB used.
fields.code_commit_hash: string, Git commit hash of the code used.
fields.dataset_commit_hash: string, Git or data version hash of the corpora and question sets.
fields.config: JSON object containing temperature, top_k, chunk_size, filters, hardware details, etc.

fields.gold_citations: array of {document_id: string, span: string or null}.
fields.agent_citations: array of {document_id: string, span: string or null}.
fields.retrieved_docs: array of {document_id: string, score: float, rank: int}.

evaluation.notes: string, optional qualitative comments by evaluator.
